clue.text: Display top competition horse

parts.note: to display something is to show it
a top is a garment worn on the upper body, such as a jumper (British for a pullover sweater)

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on view the finest animal in the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' reads as 'best' but is the garment: a JUMPER is the British word for a pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse trained to clear fences in an arena event is called by this name.

clue.text: Also housed party in London

indicators.note: partly says only part of the words before it is used, a run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Also lodged in part in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as read has 'party', which gives no indicator; 'partly' hides the district across 'alSO HOused'.
explanation.definitionFit: The West End district famous for nightlife is a place in the capital.

clue.text: Geriatric antique French polisher

parts.note: antique means old
someone who polishes furniture buffs it, so is a buffer

explanation.surface: An elderly craftsman who restores antique furniture with French polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French polisher' is a furniture finisher, not a Frenchman. An 'old buffer' is a British term for a fuddy-duddy old man.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly, old-fashioned man, informally, is a geriatric.

clue.text: So in the first month he set sail in the Argo

definitions.text: he set sail in the Argo

indicators.note: one word placed inside the abbreviation of the month

parts.note: Jan is short for January
taken as written

explanation.surface: The hero who sailed in the Argo did so in January.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero led the Argonauts on the ship Argo in quest of the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Fellow leaves to find exotic fruits

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A man departs to seek tropical produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical stone fruits with orange flesh are exotic fruits.

clue.text: No tea is produced in Eastern Europe

indicators.note: produced means made, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: No tea is grown in the eastern part of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges NO TEA IS; the definition is loose, naming a country in Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic country lies in north-eastern Europe.

clue.text: If beheaded its sting would be even more venomous

definitions.text: If beheaded its sting would be even more venomous

parts.words: If beheaded its sting would be even more venomous
parts.note: the stinging insect, losing its first letter, leaves the name of a deadly snake, whose bite is far worse

explanation.surface: A grim thought about decapitating a stinging creature and making it deadlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first letter and ASP remains, the venomous snake associated with Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-and-black stinging insect becomes a poisonous serpent when its head letter goes.

clue.text: More or less define a long session at the bar

definitions.text: a long session at the bar
definitions.meaning: a spell of drinking, split as a bout

explanation.surface: Roughly describing a lengthy drinking spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into A BOUT, a session of drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means approximately; split, it is a single spell or bout of drinking.

clue.text: Arrange for goods to be delivered

definitions.meaning: place a request for supplies, read as put in an order

explanation.surface: Organise a delivery of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to sort tidily, and read differently, to place a request for goods.

clue.text: Circular letter writer needs to heed impartiality

parts.note: O is the round letter
a pen is a writing instrument
to mind is to heed

explanation.surface: Someone writing a round-robin letter must stay fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unprejudiced and receptive, with no bias, is impartiality.

clue.text: Conceals animal skins

definitions.meaning: pelts taken from beasts, used for leather

explanation.surface: Someone tucks away pelts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for keeping out of view and a plural noun for pelts.

clue.text: Still short of the target-through incompetence?

definitions.text: Still short of the target-through incompetence?

parts.words: Still short of the target-through incompetence?
parts.note: literally not yet reaching a mark set; idiomatically lacking the ability to cope

explanation.surface: Someone failing to hit a goal, perhaps because they lack the skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lacking the capacity or fitness for a task, read literally as not having reached a level.

clue.text: Reject an appeal to lower the volume

definitions.text: an appeal to lower the volume
definitions.meaning: a request to make a radio or music quieter

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a plea to make the music quieter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both decline and reduce the setting of a sound control.

clue.text: Comment on a dowdy woman is quite unacceptable

definitions.meaning: a remark that she would not be fancied, she is not attractive at all
British colloquial for not allowed, out of order

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a frumpy woman is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang: something 'not on' is unacceptable; the first reading is a crude verdict that she does not appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means not permissible, and jokingly a dismissive verdict on someone's looks.

clue.text: A haze of whisky vapour

parts.note: a fanciful picture of steam from a Highland spirit, really the name for a thick drizzly fog in Scotland

explanation.surface: A cloud of spirit fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch is also whisky; the phrase means a fine wet mist typical of the Scottish hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names thick fine drizzle, a damp haze, playfully pictured as rising from the spirit.

clue.text: Tender-hearted chartered surveyor from the treasury

indicators.note: the word with a heart means the following abbreviation takes the other piece into its middle

parts.note: CS is an abbreviation for chartered surveyor
to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted professional surveyor working for the national exchequer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender-hearted' looks like 'kind', but 'Tender' is OFFER and 'hearted' puts it at the heart of CS.
explanation.definitionFit: The chests of money held by a government or organisation form its funds, its treasury.

clue.text: Playing Shylock is most arduous

definitions.meaning: Shylock in The Merchant of Venice demands his pound of flesh

explanation.surface: Acting the moneylender in Shakespeare is very demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means extremely demanding, and describes demanding payment like Shylock.

clue.text: One who flies over a Roman road to the right

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: A pilot passes above an ancient Roman highway heading right.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aeroplane is someone who flies.

clue.text: Sales are not too bad at the business show

parts.note: trade is buying and selling
fair means reasonable, middling

explanation.surface: Business at the commercial exhibition is reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition where companies display products is a business show.

clue.text: Country from which the monarch travels by rail

indicators.note: the monarch riding the train means her letters are placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: to go by rail is to go by train
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A land described as the one across which the queen goes by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels by' puts the monarch inside the vehicle. 'Country' means a type of land, as in open country, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of land or ground, as in hilly country, is a stretch of ground.

clue.text: Water pollutant can raise water charge

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it from bottom to top, so it is backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
water rates are the charge for water supply in Britain

explanation.surface: A contaminant in water might push up utility bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertiliser runoff salts of this kind contaminate rivers, so it is a water pollutant.

clue.text: Inappropriate term for notoriety

explanation.surface: An unsuitable label for disrepute.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a poor label; idiomatically a poor reputation, being known for the wrong reasons.

clue.text: Rough bristle makes skin sore

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughed up and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A coarse bristle causes a sore on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluid-filled bubble on the skin from friction is a skin sore.

clue.text: Uplift for one in a huge crowd

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for a large crowd

parts.note: a host is a great multitude, as in a host of angels
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being lifted up while in a vast throng, like crowd-surfing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising something up with a lift or crane is an uplift.

clue.text: Expose oneself to some heroin cure

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking a drug treatment may leave one vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a risk or penalty on oneself is to expose oneself to it.

clue.text: Sturdy members of the bottom stream

definitions.meaning: a school group of the dimmest pupils, 'thick' being British slang for stupid and a 'set' a class grouping

explanation.surface: Solidly built people who are in the lowest class at school.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stream' is a British school ability grouping; read as THICK SET, the dull pupils' group.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocky, broadly built person is sturdy; split, the phrase names a class of slow learners.

clue.text: It sounds like a calmer destiny

indicators.note: the clue says outright that what follows is spoken and resembles the answer

parts.note: more tranquil; in a non-rhotic British accent it is said like the answer

explanation.surface: Fate seemingly being more serene.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in British pronunciation, where the R of 'calmer' is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist belief, the accumulated effect of deeds shapes one's fate.

clue.text: Patient cry uttered by chemist's radical group

indicators.note: uttered tells us the words are spoken out loud and only the sound counts

parts.note: a sick patient might cry I'm ill

explanation.surface: A patient's call heard by a pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: A complaining patient's cry is 'I'm ill', which said quickly sounds like the chemical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-carbon alkyl group, C5H11, is a radical group in chemistry.

clue.text: Liaising in swindle requires diplomacy

parts.note: a con is a swindle or fraud
tact is sensitivity and diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Coordinating within a fraudulent scheme takes careful handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in communication with someone, connecting with them, is liaising.

clue.text: Domain of a true male

parts.note: real means genuine or true

explanation.surface: The territory belonging to a genuine man.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or sphere of rule is a domain.

clue.text: Act resulting in revolution

definitions.meaning: a stage routine or performance, as in a variety show

explanation.surface: Behaviour that leads to an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a music-hall performer's routine and one full rotation.

clue.text: It could contain what a real Berber brewed

definitions.text: It could contain what a real Berber brewed

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so the letters of these two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cask that might hold whatever ale a genuine North African has made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges REAL BERBER; the whole clue also describes the cask that would hold home brew.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask for storing ale would hold what was brewed.
